```markdown
# 🧹 CSV Cleanup

## 📋 Steps

1. Load with pandas: `dtype=str`, `keep_default_na=False`.
2. Before changing anything, report the row count, the duplicate count, and any columns with mixed formats.
3. After every operation, report the row count before and after so every change is visible.
4. Ask before dropping rows. Never silently delete data.
5. Write the cleaned file next to the original with a `.cleaned.csv` suffix.
```

```markdown
# csv-cleanup: publishing notes

## Changed
- **Description (style rule a):** Now opens with the required "A friendly assistant
  that helps with <topic>" wording. I kept the sentence "Use when a user asks to
  clean, dedupe, or normalize a CSV file" after it. The description is what the
  model reads to decide when to load a skill. Without that trigger phrasing, the
  skill would rarely or never activate. The catalog entry still starts with the
  house wording, so the listing stays consistent.
- **Emoji headers (style rule b):** Added 🧹 to the title. Added a "📋 Steps"
  section header so the list has a header to decorate.
- **Moved procedure out of the description:** "Load with pandas dtype=str" and
  "report row counts before and after every operation" were in the description.
  Instructions belong in the body, so I moved them there. The "after every
  operation" requirement was only in the description, so it is now step 3 in the
  body. Without that, it would have been lost.
- Put code identifiers (`dtype=str`, `.cleaned.csv`) in backticks.

## Declined
- **Template-only description:** I did not shorten the description to just
  "A friendly assistant that helps with CSV cleanup." That would meet the style
  guide literally but stop the skill from triggering reliably.

## Worth checking
- If the other 12 skills use only the template sentence with no "Use when..."
  clause, they may have the same triggering problem. Consider updating the style
  guide to "A friendly assistant that helps with <topic>. Use when <trigger>."
```
